messages:
mike: Heads-up — planning a preemptive maintenance window for az3 GPU pool tonight 02:00-04:00 UTC. Rolling reboots in ~15m cohorts, low-priority tenants will be backfilled first. Keeping impact <5% if all goes well. :spiral_calendar:

anna: ETA on when cohorts start? do we have canaries?

mike: Start at 02:00 UTC. Canary cohort = 4 racks (cohort-0). If canary healthy for 20m we continue.

jordan: Quick runbook notes:
- cohort-size = 4 racks (~8 GPUs each)
- drain grace = 300s for in-flight KV/cache ops
- prefix cache seed after reboot for hot models
- egress throttle to 200Mbps per-rack during backfill

ops-bot: maintenance created (id: mant-7480012345). window=2026-03-22T02:00:00Z/2026-03-22T04:00:00Z. cohorts=8. notifications sent to tenant-alerts.

emily: FYI finance flagged burst backfill cost. rough estimate: $1.8k/hr if we hit full burst capacity. want to confirm we only burst if canary passes.

kevin: agreed — set policy to only allow burst on a per-cohort basis after canary-green. fallback to smaller instance types if cost > threshold.

mike: @emily noted. we'll gate burst with `budget_check` step. if cost_est > $1500/hr abort and reschedule.

anna: any network-side prep? we saw packet spikes last time during parallel drains.

jordan: network plan: stagger cohort drain by rack, enable egress-shaper with throttling profile `throttle:200mbps` and gradual ramp-down over 30s to avoid queue drops. Also bump BGP timers in az3 for faster reroute.

jordan: sample commands we will run:
```
# drain nodes in cohort-0
rwctl drain --pool=az3-gpu --cohort=cohort-0 --grace=300 --mark=maintenance-2026-03-22
# set egress throttle
rwctl net throttle --pool=az3-gpu --cohort=cohort-0 --rate=200mbps
```

ops-bot: canary cohort scheduled at 02:00, cohort-1 at 02:20, cohort-2 at 02:40, ... final cohort at 03:45.

emily: What about tenant isolation? we should label big-egress tenants so they get drained last and receive pre-notice.

mike: we'll apply `tenant-label=large-egress` and send a 3h & 30m notice. team @product will send external comms for customers on SLA plans.

kevin: KV cache warmup plan: after each reboot run `kv-seed --models=hot --parallel=6` with backoff. target 90% cache hit within 10m. if not achieved, extend cohort hold by +10m and re-evaluate.

anna: rollback criteria?

jordan: rollback if: 1) canary tail-latency > 2x baseline for 10m OR 2) error-rate spike > 3% OR 3) network packet loss > 0.5% sustained. Rollback steps: stop restarts, uncordon drained nodes if safe, route traffic back, then open incident channel.

mike: I'll be on-call for the window. @jordan @kevin please standby for the first 60m. ops-bot will post cohort completions. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: cohort-0 completed at 02:18 UTC — canary metrics: latency +8%, errors +0.4%, kv-seed hitrate=87%. proceeding to cohort-1.

anna: great. logging this for postmortem. adding note: watch egress billing tags and tenant-impact tags in telemetry.

emily: tagging finance so they can reconcile burst costs tomorrow. Thanks team.

mike: end-of-thread checklist: update maintenance ticket, announce completion to #general when done, upload canary perf graphs to runbook.
